key_insight: A continuous-variable flag oscillator can record ancilla decay as a measurable phase-space shift, allowing feedback to undo continuous errors on bosonic codes.
engineering_relevance: This gives hybrid qubit-oscillator platforms a practical way to suppress ancilla-induced gate errors using only standard dispersive couplings, displacements, rotations, and heterodyne readout.
method: Couple a flag oscillator to the ancilla so decay-induced errors are mapped into the flag's phase-space position.
Heterodyne-measure the flag after the gate to estimate the continuous error.
Apply feedback to correct the storage mode, up to a bosonic code stabilizer.
evidence_signal: Simulations with realistic circuit-QED parameters report more than three orders of magnitude fewer logical errors for a four-component cat-code parity measurement and a GKP logical lifetime near the noiseless-ancilla limit.
watch_item: The approach still depends on accurate flag readout and feedback, and the correction is designed around specific gate sequences and error models.
paper_title: Protecting bosonic codes from ancilla-induced errors with continuous-variable flags
